Identical logic applies to NAGS LoF (NAGS makes the CPS1 activator N-acetylglutamate) and OTC LoF. do(CPS1 LoF) → urea cycle blocked → urea production ↓ → BUN ↓.

causal:influence:erythrocyte_methemoglob.evidence: Hereditary methemoglobinemia types I and II (OMIM #250800): CYB5R3 LoF raises erythrocyte metHb to 10-70%; patients are cyanotic with reduced true oxyhemoglobin saturation (Percy & Lappin 2008 Lancet 371:2032). Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Methemoglobinaemia': metHb fraction directly reduces O2-carrying capacity and SaO2. Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology, 'Haemoglobin and O2 transport': functional Hb = total Hb minus metHb; SaO2 (true) falls proportionally to metHb fraction. Intervention: genetic LoF CYB5R3 (OMIM #250800) — erythrocyte metHb rises, SaO2 falls; pharmacological methemoglobin-inducing agents (dapsone, nitrites) phenocopy. | intervention: Genetic LoF: homozygous CYB5R3 mutation (OMIM #250800, recessive congenital methemoglobinemia types I/II) — erythrocyte methemoglobin rises to 10-70% of total haemoglobin, producing cyanosis and reduced arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythrocyte_methemoglob.mechanism: Methemoglobin (Fe3+ haem) cannot bind molecular oxygen and does not participate in O2 transport. When the erythrocyte methemoglobin fraction rises, the proportion of functional oxyhaemoglobin (Fe2+ haem) available at any alveolar PO2 is correspondingly reduced, lowering arterial SaO2. Additionally, methemoglobin allosterically shifts the O2-dissociation curve of the remaining Fe2+ haem leftward (higher O2 affinity, impaired O2 unloading), but the dominant acute effect is the direct reduction in O2-carrying haemoglobin fraction. In hereditary methemoglobinemia (CYB5R3 LoF, OMIM 250800), metHb rises to 10-70% of total haemoglobin and patients present with cyanosis and reduced functional SaO2. do(CYB5R3 LoF) => erythrocyte_methemoglobin UP => hemoglobin_o2_saturation DOWN.

causal:influence:monoamine_oxidase_activ.evidence: Robinson DS 1975 Fed Proc 34:103: MAO activity inversely correlates with CSF dopamine metabolites across age; Fowler JS et al 1997 PNAS 94:4938 — MAO-B inhibition raises brain dopamine levels. | intervention: do(monoamine_oxidase_activity -) — selegiline/rasagiline MAO-B inhibition raises synaptic and CSF dopamine; do(monoamine_oxidase_activity +) — no direct pharmacological up-regulation, but loss-of-function MAO mutations (Brunner syndrome, OMIM 300615) markedly elevate dopamine and CSF dopamine. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:monoamine_oxidase_activ.mechanism: Monoamine oxidase (MAO-A and MAO-B) catalyses the oxidative deamination of dopamine in presynaptic neurons and astroglia to 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, which is further oxidised to DOPAC and then HVA. causal:influence:suox_activity:positive:.mechanism: Sulfite oxidase (SUOX) oxidises sulfite to sulfate, the terminal step of cysteine/methionine catabolism.
